subject: GRB 260808A: NuSTAR detection of prompt emission
body:
G. Waratkar (Caltech) and B. Grefenstette (Caltech) report on behalf of the NuSTAR Search for INteresting Gamma-ray Signals (SINGS) working group:

The NuSTAR SINGS working group reports the detection of prompt emission from the long-duration GRB 260808A in both the NuSTAR CsI anti-coincidence shields. Details of the search algorithm will be described in a future paper.

The NuSTAR SINGS algorithm, triggered at 2026-08-08T02:51:42.310 UTC, shows a detection of GRB 260808A, also detected by Fermi-GBM (GCN 45313).

The NuSTAR CsI shield data are recorded at 1 Hz. We detect a single episode with two peaks lasting for about 20-s. The peak count rate is ~1500-cps with a baseline rate of ~1000-cps during this time period. We do not see any evidence in the signal above 100 keV in the CZT detectors.

The Fermi-GBM localization (GCN 45313) at RA = 341.8, Dec = 14.1 implies an offset from the NuSTAR boresight of 76-deg (i.e. from the side) and an offset from the geocenter of 135-deg.

Lightcurves and analysis for this GRB can be found here:
https://nustarsoc.caltech.edu/NuSTAR_Public/grbs/reports/2026/260808A 

Information on NuSTAR SINGS can be found here: 
https://nustarsoc.caltech.edu/NuSTAR_Public/grbs/     

NuSTAR is a NASA Small Explorer mission led by Caltech and managed by JPL for NASA's Science Mission Directorate in Washington.
